name: The Caucasian Wingnut of the Zuiderpark Collection
access: Free. Public street planting (plantsoen), open at any time.
transport: About 2 km south of Tilburg station.
verify_notes: Register (LRMB, netherlands-lrmb.json nr 1697210) is the only source that names this specific tree; existence/species/age are single-sourced from it, hence flagged. Register's own name is 'Japanse vleugelnoot' (literally 'Japanese wingnut') but its mapped species field is Caucasian Wingnut, Pterocarya fraxinifolia; note the naming mismatch for the writer, the species field is the one to trust. Planted band 1950-1960, so roughly 66-76 years old as of 2026: young for this project but the register flags it for rarity and cultural history rather than age. Part of a documented rare-tree teaching collection: register history says this ringed the former municipal nursery (gemeentekwekerij) on the Tatraweg, planted from 1950 to teach evening horticulture and floristry students, and from 1953 to 1967 some 800-1000 students a season learned the Latin and Dutch names of the trees along a path nicknamed the 'zweetlaantje' (sweat lane) where they were examined. From 1967 the teaching moved to the Lagere Agrarische Sierteeltschool on Leijparkweg; that school's 1967 opening date and later 1974 merger into Scholengemeenschap Quirijn are independently confirmed on wikimiddenbrabant.nl (Wiki Midden-Brabant, a local heemkunde wiki), which corroborates the shared historical narrative though not this individual tree. No independent recent 'still alive' confirmation was found this pass beyond the register entry itself; no vitality field exists in any register. Setting is 'plantsoen' (public street verge in the Zuiderpark residential area), owner_category gemeente, register's own visitable=ja and visible=ja. This is one of five trees from the same collection verified this pass, forming a new walkable cluster (all within about 300 m of each other) roughly 1.2-1.4 km from the Tilburg city centre, distinct from the existing Wilhelminapark and Leijpark clusters already published.

name: The American Yellowwood of the Zuiderpark Collection
access: Free. Public street planting (plantsoen), open at any time.
transport: About 2 km south of Tilburg station.
verify_notes: Register (LRMB nr 1697211, register_name 'Geelhout Zuiderpark') is the only source naming this specific tree, hence flagged. Register gives no species field ('species_unmapped: Geelhout'); 'geelhout' is the standard Dutch common name for Cladrastis kentukea (American Yellowwood / Kentucky yellowwood), confirmed against multiple independent Dutch nursery and dendrology references (boomzorg.nl, Ebben Tree Nursery, bomengids.nl) that this pass checked for the species mapping only, not for this individual tree's existence. Planted band 1950-1960, so roughly 66-76 years old as of 2026. Multi-stemmed ('Meerstammig' in the register). Same rare-tree teaching-collection history as the other Zuiderpark entries this pass (see til_008's verify_notes for the full anecdote about the gemeentekwekerij and the 1950s-60s horticulture evening school); that shared narrative's founding dates are independently corroborated via wikimiddenbrabant.nl, though not this specific tree. No independent recent alive-confirmation found beyond the register. Setting 'plantsoen', owner gemeente, register visitable=ja, visible=ja. Yellowwood flowers in May/June with drooping white racemes and turns yellow in autumn; worth a best_time note for the writer if a source narrows the local bloom timing.

Same address (Morvanstraat 14) as til_008 (Caucasian Wingnut) and the blocked Eikbladige beuk (see blocked list), a few metres apart.

name: The Golden Beech of the Zuiderpark Collection
access: Free. Public street planting (plantsoen), open at any time.
transport: About 2 km south of Tilburg station.
verify_notes: Register (LRMB nr 1697209, register_name 'Goudbeuk Zuiderpark') is the only source naming this specific tree, hence flagged. 'Goudbeuk' is confirmed by multiple independent Dutch nursery references (Appeltern, dendrologie.nl, Limburgplant) as the standard Dutch name for Fagus sylvatica 'Zlatia', a golden-leaved beech cultivar whose leaves emerge yellow in spring, turn yellow-green in summer and yellow again in autumn. Planted band 1950-1960, roughly 66-76 years old as of 2026. Same rare-tree teaching-collection history as til_008-011 (see til_008's verify_notes). No independent recent alive-confirmation found beyond the register. Setting 'plantsoen', owner gemeente, register visitable=ja, visible=ja. Good best_time candidate: spring leaf-out (April-May) when the crown is brightest gold, fading toward yellow-green by midsummer; a writer could set best_time kind 'fresh leaves' for April/May but should not narrow the month further than a real source supports.

name: The Kloosterpark Oak

location.address: Leijpark, Kloosterpark corner, far northeast of the park off Ringbaan-Zuid

transport: About 2.5 km southeast of Tilburg station.
verify_notes: Register (LRMB nr 1695664, register_name 'kloosterparkeik', which literally means 'cloister-park oak') is the only source naming this specific tree; the register itself gives no species beyond 'oak', so the page should ask the reader which oak this is rather than guess pedunculate vs sessile. Planted band 1900-1910, roughly 116-126 years old as of 2026, older than this. This is a different, older sub-cluster of the Leijpark from the one that produced the already-published til_005/til_006: it sits in the extreme northeast corner, in the 'Kloosterparkbos', a wood that originally belonged to the neighbouring convent of the Congregatie van Onze Lieve Vrouw der Afzondering in het Cenakel (founded 1908); as the convent's grounds were redeveloped the wood passed to municipal management and was folded into the Leijpark, whose own path network now runs through it. Two tall black residential towers stand beside it, built in the former convent garden. The register's own history for the wider Leijpark (30 hectares, designed 1919 by Leonard Springer, built 1934-1939 as an unemployment work-relief project after land-acquisition delays) is independently corroborated by nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leijpark, which confirms designer, area, and the 1934-1939 build under the same work-relief circumstances; Wikipedia does not mention the Kloosterpark/convent detail specifically, so that part rests on the register alone. No independent recent alive-confirmation found beyond the register; no vitality field in any register. Setting 'park', owner gemeente. This tree, til_014 (kloosterparklinde) and til_015 (kloosterparkhulst) sit within about 30 metres of each other, an easy joint stop when extending the existing Leijpark walk further northeast.
